reason: The root bed needs clean granules, so firing the graded material seems like the first preparation.
expectation: The kiln will turn the regolith into mineral granules; I don't yet know how they will be cleaned.

alternatives.reason: Mixing nutrients looks useful for feeding the roots, but I want to prepare their bed first.

effect: Firing produced porous granules, so I can now wash them before using them as a bed.
reaction: The porous result fits the need for air around roots, which is satisfying.
reason: Water should wash soluble material from the granules before they reach the troughs.
expectation: The granules will be washed, though I don't know whether one wash will be enough.

alternatives.reason: The nutrient solution is also needed, but I want to finish preparing the granules first.

effect: The wash made growing granules, and the offered test suggests checking what still leaches out.
reaction: I am curious whether washing was sufficient.
reason: Testing the washed granules seems sensible before putting them near roots.
expectation: The cell will check material leaching from the granules, possibly identifying whether they are clean enough.

effect: The test confirms a clean batch and explains the granules support roots while imported nutrients feed them.
reaction: I like the distinction between support and nutrition, although the test itself gave no measurement.
reason: The clean granules belong in the lined troughs to make the growing bed.
expectation: The troughs will be filled with clean granules, ready for the nutrient solution.

effect: The granules are now in root troughs, so the solution is the remaining obvious preparation.
reaction: The assembly was straightforward; nothing surprising.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should dilute the concentrate for the plants.
expectation: It will make a nutrient solution suitable for the troughs.

effect: The nutrient solution is ready to add to the mineral troughs.
reason: The only offered combination should provide water and food to the prepared root bed.
expectation: The solution will be added to the troughs, leaving space for air around roots.

effect: The irrigated troughs complete the setup, with circulation inserts and separate spaces for lettuce and potatoes.
reaction: The two intended crops make the finished object feel useful, though the air supply appears through supplied inserts rather than an action I understood in detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the washed granules and learning they provide physical support while imported nutrients feed the roots made the purpose of the medium clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mixing water and concentrate was predictable and gave no detail about the measurement mentioned in the introduction.

surprise.text: The finished troughs have supplied circulation inserts; I had not seen how air would be provided until the end.

arbitrary.text: The leach test has a clear purpose, but the result gives no indication of what was measured or why the batch passed.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see the crops grow and how the station develops, though this chapter's combinations were mostly straightforward.
